reason: I have been telling clients we 'do automation' for a year with nobody to actually build it, and a 150 EUR form-to-CRM I can resell at 500 is exactly the gap. The free first task costs me nothing but an afternoon, so I will try it on one real job and see if the work and the deadline hold.
objection: One person, 10-12 hours a week, a day job, university exams, 'two tasks at a time' - that is the profile of the freelancer who vanished on me two days before launch. If he gets a busy month at the Oracle job, my client's deadline is the thing that slips, under my brand. And honestly the grant-funded angle is not the draw; those clients pay late and bury you in paperwork, I would rather use him for normal SME automation.
would_change_my_mind: A named backup person or a written guarantee of what happens when a deadline is missed (refund plus who finishes the work). Without that it stays a 150 EUR experiment, never a service I put on my price list.
